record.paper_title: D-symmetric operators: comments and some open problems
record.context_brief: Norm-closedness of compact perturbations of D-symmetric operators
record.original_question: Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space and let L(H) be the algebra of bounded linear operators on H. If an operator T in L(H) is called D-symmetric when the norm closure of the range of δ_T(X)=TX-XT equals the norm closure of the range of δ_{T*}, and if K denotes a compact operator on H, is the set {T+K : T is D-symmetric and K is compact} norm-closed in L(H)?

evidence.quote: Definition 2.1. An operator A ∈ L(H) is called D-symmetric, if R(δA) = R(δA∗ ).
Now we will recall the following question posed by Joel Anderson et.al [2]. Is the set {T + K : T, D-symmetric, K compact } norm-closed in L(H)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, and let $L(H)$ denote the algebra of bounded linear operators on $H$. For $T \in L(H)$, define the inner derivation $\delta_T : L(H) \to L(H)$ by $\delta_T(X) = TX - XT$. Call an operator $T \in L(H)$ *D-symmetric* if the norm closure of the range of $\delta_T$ equals the norm closure of the range of $\delta_{T^*}$, i.e. $\overline{\mathrm{Ran}(\delta_T)} = \overline{\mathrm{Ran}(\delta_{T^*})}$. Let $K(H)$ denote the ideal of compact operators on $H$. Determine whether the set
$$\{T + K : T \in L(H) \text{ is D-symmetric},\ K \in K(H)\}$$
is norm-closed in $L(H)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question, originally posed by J. Anderson and collaborators, asks whether the set of compact perturbations of D-symmetric operators is norm-closed in L(H). It is listed as an open problem in surveys on D-symmetric operators, and no published resolution was located in the search.
